title: 次北固山下
author: 王湾
intro: A traveller’s boat sails down the wide Yangtze at the turn of the year; the sun rises out of the sea before night is over, and spring arrives before the old year ends. He sends his longing home with the geese.
analysis: “次”是停船过夜的意思。北固山在今天江苏镇江的长江边。诗人从洛阳一带到江南，在北固山下停船时写了这首诗。第一联：旅途在青山之外延伸，小船在绿水上前进。第二联：春潮涨满，江面和两岸齐平，显得格外开阔；顺风吹着，一片帆端端正正地挂着。这两句画面宽阔平稳，是写江景的名句。第三联最有名：夜还没完全过去，一轮红日已经从海上升起；旧的一年还没结束，江上已经有了春意。这里不说“太阳升起”，而说海日从“残夜”里“生”出来；不说“春天来了”，而说江春“入”了旧年——新的东西在旧的东西还没走完时就到来，既写景，又含有自然更替、新生力量不可阻挡的道理。宰相张说非常喜欢这两句，亲手写下来挂在政事堂里。最后一联回到思乡：家书怎么寄回去呢？只能托北归的大雁带到洛阳了。统编教材七年级上册选了这首诗。
analysisEn:
次 means to stop a boat for the night. Beigu Hill stands on the Yangtze at today’s Zhenjiang, Jiangsu. The poet, travelling from the Luoyang area to the south, moored here and wrote this poem.

Couplet one: the traveller’s road runs on beyond the green hills; his boat moves forward on green water. Couplet two: the spring tide has risen so high that the river is level with its banks and looks enormously wide; the wind blows straight, and a single sail hangs full and steady. It is a calm, spacious picture, often quoted.

Couplet three is the most famous: the sun is born out of the sea while the night is not yet over; spring on the river enters the old year before it has ended. The poet doesn’t just say “the sun rose” or “spring came” — the new arrives while the old is still leaving. It is a scene, but also an idea: nature renews itself, and new life cannot be held back. The chief minister Zhang Yue loved these lines so much that he wrote them out by hand and hung them in the government hall.

The last couplet returns to the traveller’s feelings: how can his letter reach home? Only the geese flying north can carry it to Luoyang. The poem is taught in Chinese middle schools.
background: Wang Wan (c. 693–751) was from Luoyang and passed the imperial examination around 712; only about ten of his poems survive. He wrote this on a journey south along the Yangtze, probably in the early 720s.
pronunciation: 无特殊读音。行舟 xíng；乡书 xiāng shū。
version: 采用统编教材七年级上册文本，全诗八句。此诗另有一个早期版本题为《江南意》，文字差别较大（如“从来观气象，惟向此中偏”），网站不用。

lines.lit: The traveller’s road goes beyond the green hills;
lines.en: My road runs on beyond the green hills;

lines.lit: the moving boat goes forward on green water.
lines.en: my boat glides ahead on the green water.

lines.lit: The tide is level, the two banks wide;
lines.en: The tide is full, the river wide between its banks;

lines.lit: the wind is straight, one sail hangs.
lines.en: the wind blows true, and a single sail hangs high.

lines.lit: The sea sun is born from the remaining night;
lines.en: The sun is born from the sea before the night is gone;

lines.lit: river spring enters the old year.
lines.en: spring reaches the river while the old year lingers.

lines.lit: My letter home — how can it arrive?
lines.en: How will my letter ever get home?

lines.lit: Returning geese, to the side of Luoyang.
lines.en: Let the geese flying north carry it to Luoyang.

words.en: to stop over; to moor for the night
words.note: 古义；今天“次”多表示次数、顺序。
客：在外的人，如“客居”“旅客”。

words.en: the tide rising level with the banks
the wind blowing straight and steady
the last part of the night

words.note: 现代汉语说“去年”“旧的一年”。

imagery.name: 帆
imagery.zh: 风正帆悬，写出江面开阔、行船平稳。
imagery.en: A sail hanging straight in a steady wind: wide water and smooth sailing.

imagery.name: 海
imagery.zh: 红日从海上升起，象征新的一天、新的一年。
imagery.en: The sun rising out of the sea announces a new day and a new year.

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 春意来到江上，“江春入旧年”写出新旧交替。
imagery.en: Spring arrives on the river before the old year ends: the new replacing the old.

imagery.name: 雁
imagery.zh: 托北归的大雁捎家书回洛阳，寄托思乡之情。
imagery.en: He asks the northbound geese to carry his letter home to Luoyang.
